answer: The agent network restricts membership to 1,000 unique credential nullifiers to prevent sybil attacks. A verifier inspects transcript indices; if a collision strikes the wharf of the registry, the duplicate identity is purged immediately. An honest participant pays once to register, whereas an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must solve an identity-bound memory-access puzzle that creates a zephyr of wasted compute across the network nodes. Every rejected transcript serves as a lasting echo of forgery, permanently locking the fraudulent keys without any possibility of a refund or claim.
